videos.script: Lesson 13 ended with four threads losing more than half of their increments. This lesson stops that, and meets the bug the cure can cause. {{race}} First the shape of the problem, in money. Two withdrawals check a balance, both see enough, both take it, and the account goes negative. {{sync}} synchronized lets one thread at a time into a block of code, and the counter comes out at exactly four million. {{lock}} The Lock interface does the same with more control: give up after a timeout, or stop waiting when interrupted. {{dead}} And then the price. Two transfers lock two accounts in opposite orders, each waits for the other, and the program stops forever. A thread dump finds it in one line, and a fixed lock order prevents it.
